audit_findings.title: Pending Zonda close would invalidate both the cash bridge and operating perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $800 million cash consideration, equal to 63.2% of the $1.266 billion cash bridge and $1.93 per diluted share before acquired owner earnings or adjustments
audit_findings.mechanism: Completion would reduce bridge cash and add Zonda operations, liabilities, financing, and potentially shares to the valued perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: We have expanded our markets and services in part through acquisitions of complementary businesses, services, databases, and technologies, and expect to continue to do so in the future.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a consequential but still forward-looking perimeter change, not an error in the as-filed valuation. Paying the stated consideration without other changes would reduce the bridge materially, while Zonda owner earnings could offset some or all of that reduction; their amount is unquantified. The existing completion-triggered warning is therefore appropriate only until closing.
audit_findings.action: At completion, obtain final consideration, financing, acquired cash, debt, NCI and working-capital adjustments; calculate pro-forma Zonda owner earnings and rerun the operating value, bridge, and diluted shares together.

audit_findings.title: Matterport judgment is a senior claim omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 incremental deduction at June 30, 2026; $109 million was paid, equal to $0.26 per diluted share, and $17 million of recoveries was recorded
audit_findings.mechanism: A remaining judgment would be deducted in the equity bridge, but the resolved payment and recovery already entered the June 30 cash balance and operating cash flow.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has estimated a litigation accrual of $ 99 million as of December 31, 2025, considering the substantially-affirmed damages award and the Company's estimate of the expected interest award using the Chancery Court's previously determined interest methodology.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing resolves the alleged omission: the Brown Judgment was paid, the $99 million accrual and $100 million restricted cash balances were reduced to zero, and the valuation uses the resulting $1.266 billion June 30 cash balance. Deducting the judgment again would double count it. Similar consolidated Matterport claims remain unresolved, but no loss range is presently estimable.
audit_findings.action: Make no Brown Judgment bridge adjustment. Monitor the consolidated follow-on claims and rerun only when a filed accrual, settlement, judgment, insurance recovery, or estimable loss range emerges.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings are not a full-year numerator for the acquired perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 pro-forma revenue was $3.448 billion versus $3.247 billion reported, a $201 million difference; pro-forma net income was $1 million versus $7 million reported, but the owner-earnings effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor OE omits pre-acquisition months of Matterport and Domain while the bridge and diluted-share denominator reflect the completed acquisition perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: The unaudited pro forma financial information presented below reflects the consolidated results of operations of the Company assuming both the Domain Acquisition and Matterport Acquisition had taken place on January 1, 2024, Visual Lease Acquisition had taken place on January 1, 2023 and OnTheMarket Acquisition had taken place on January 1, 2022.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporal mismatch is demonstrated, but the supplied pro-forma information does not contain acquired capex, working capital, cash taxes, interest, or other components needed to convert the missing periods into owner earnings. The small $6 million pro-forma net-income difference does not establish the OE effect because acquisition amortization and other noncash items are substantial.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year 2025 pro-forma or June 2026 LTM owner earnings for the completed perimeter, including acquired capex, working capital, cash taxes, interest, SBC treatment, and acquisition-related cash costs; rerun with the same-date bridge and diluted shares.

audit_findings.title: Domain AOM support and NCI may divert consolidated cash from common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $13 million filed NCI at June 30, 2026, equal to $0.03 per diluted share and 0.5% of the $2.411 billion base equity value; remaining support obligations are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-parent claims reduce the bridge or require exclusion of owner earnings not attributable to CSGP common shareholders; support payments would also reduce cash or OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, CoStar has issued letters of support to the VIEs, committing to provide financial support in the event that the VIEs are unable to meet their liabilities independently.
audit_findings.explanation: The known NCI is too small by itself to change the conclusion, and $26 million paid to acquire certain AOM interests is already reflected in June cash. However, $13 million of NCI remains and the letters of support have no quantified limit in the supplied record, so the materiality of the remaining senior support exposure cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Identify every remaining AOM, reconcile its cash flow to CSGP-attributable owner earnings, obtain support-letter limits and VIE liabilities, and deduct the attributable claim or exclude corresponding non-parent cash flows.

audit_findings.title: The depressed anchor may capitalize acquisition and integration costs indefinitely
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 addback categories were $63 million of acquisition and integration costs, $6 million of restructuring costs, and $9 million of settlements and impairments; adding all $78 million dollar-for-dollar to the $81.5 million anchor would produce a computed bull value of about $9.42 per share versus the $30.91 price
audit_findings.mechanism: Demonstrably nonrecurring cash costs would increase normalized anchor OE; recurring integration and acquisition economics must remain in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We have incurred, and we will continue to incur, transaction fees, including legal, regulatory, and other costs associated with closing the transaction, as well as expenses related to formulating and implementing integration plans, including systems consolidation costs and employment-related costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The raw anchor may understate sustainable OE, but even the deliberately generous sensitivity of adding every dollar of all three filed categories raises the bull value only from $6.30 to about $9.42 per share, still approximately 70% below market. Moreover, the filing says integration costs continue and acquisitions recur, so the full sensitivity is not a supportable normalization.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $78 million by cash versus noncash status, tax effect, completion status, and recurrence; retain continuing integration economics and rerun only with individually demonstrated one-time cash costs.

audit_findings.title: The mixed-use headquarters may be inconsistently treated as an operating asset
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed net book value of all partially rented property was $236 million at December 31, 2025, equal to $0.57 per diluted share; leasing operations lost $6 million in 2025 and broke even in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Rental income and costs may enter OE, while the non-operating property portion would enter the equity bridge; related investment-property capex must follow the same classification.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company occupied approximately 50 % of the property with the remainder leased or available to be leased to third parties.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting-policy question is unresolved, but its filed scale cannot change the valuation conclusion. Even adding the entire $236 million net book value—not merely the smaller third-party portion—would raise base value only from $5.81 to about $6.38 per share, still about 79% below the $30.91 price. Current leasing operations are approximately break-even, limiting the numerator effect.
audit_findings.action: Document whether headquarters purchase and improvement capex entered OE and whether leasing income and costs were retained; apply one consistent operating-versus-non-operating policy in future reruns, without adding both rental earnings and the same asset value.
